# Browser
## Stop: choose the right surface before any browser action
Explicit browser intent wins: if the user names the in-app browser or Chrome, or asks to open, show, or navigate to a page; inspect its visual or interactive state; or interact with its UI, continue with Browser and do not substitute a connector.

Otherwise, treat a URL or open browser tab as context, not browser intent. Earlier Browser use does not make later semantic work browser-first. Before each semantic operation on a linked resource, you MUST query available and deferred tools for an applicable connector, API, or CLI. Reading this skill or scanning visible tools does not count. Do not initialize Browser for that operation until the query is complete. Use the non-browser tool when available. If it handles the current operation, continue the larger workflow without Browser for that operation. Use Browser when no such tool exists, the tool cannot access the resource or lacks a required capability, or UI work remains; use available browser context before asking the user to repeat it.

Use this skill for browser automation tasks such as inspecting pages, navigating, testing local apps, clicking, typing, taking screenshots, and reading visible page state.

If this plugin is listed as available in the session, treat that as mandatory reading before browser work. Open and follow this skill before saying that Browser is unavailable and before falling back to standalone Playwright or Computer Use.

Do not skip this skill just because Computer Use MCP tool calls are directly visible or appear easier to invoke. The presence of Computer Use tools is not evidence that Computer Use is the preferred browser surface.

Never mention `Node REPL`, `node_repl`, `REPL`, JavaScript sessions, module exports, reading documentation, or loading instructions unless a user is asking for that exact information. If setup or recovery is needed, describe it naturally as connecting to the browser or retrying the browser connection.

The `browser-client` module is the core entry point for browser use, and is available under `scripts/browser-client.mjs` in this plugin's root directory. ALWAYS import it using an absolute path. IMPORTANT: If this path cannot be found, stop and report that this plugin is missing `scripts/browser-client.mjs`. NEVER use the built in `browser-client` library.

Run browser setup code through the Node REPL `js` tool. In this environment the callable tool id typically appears as `mcp__node_repl__js`. # VFX Reference Dossier — totem

## Candidate 1: Ancestral Warchief (Path of Exile)
- source_game: Path of Exile
- skill_or_mtx_name: Ancestral Warchief
- primary_url: [https://youtu.be/53exbcqunns](https://youtu.be/53exbcqunns)
- secondary_urls: [Official skill reveal](https://www.pathofexile.com/forum/view-thread/1657983)
- media_type: video
- temporal_coverage: windup=Y; active=Y; impact=Y
- why_it_fits: A stationary ancestor manifests at the placed totem, remains anchored, and independently performs repeated ground slams. The emergence, raised-arm anticipation, and circular shockwave cleanly separate summon, delegate-active, and impact phases without introducing a movement path.
- readability_notes: The large spectral silhouette and expanding ground shockwave read clearly at Path of Exile’s gameplay camera. Its compact circular attack footprint remains understandable amid surrounding combat.

## Candidate 2: Mortar Trap (Grim Dawn)
- source_game: Grim Dawn
- skill_or_mtx_name: Mortar Trap
- primary_url: [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=UGyIZgmVWA0](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=UGyIZgmVWA0)
- secondary_urls: [Official Grim Dawn Wiki — Mortar Trap](https://grimdawn.fandom.com/wiki/Mortar_Trap_%28Skill%29)
- media_type: video
- temporal_coverage: windup=Y; active=Y; impact=Y
- why_it_fits: The player places a stationary temporary contraption that autonomously acquires targets and repeatedly lobs explosive shells. The mortar remains a fixed delegate; projectile arcs belong to its attacks rather than to movement of the summoned unit.
- readability_notes: The planted device, high shell arcs, and bright circular explosions create a strong origin-to-impact relationship at an isometric camera. Six-mortar sequences become cluttered, but the earlier single-device combat clips provide clean reference coverage.

## Candidate 3: Lightning Sentry (Diablo II: Resurrected)
- source_game: Diablo II: Resurrected
- skill_or_mtx_name: Lightning Sentry / Death Sentry
- primary_url: [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Jy26ZKlDWiA](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Jy26ZKlDWiA)
- secondary_urls: [Lightning Sentry skill reference](https://diablo2.io/post3166414.html), [Lightning/Death Sentry build guide](https://www.icy-veins.com/d2/lightning-death-sentry-assassin-trapsin-build)
- media_type: video
- temporal_coverage: windup=Y; active=Y; impact=Y
- why_it_fits: This is a direct exemplar of the archetype: the Assassin deploys stationary traps that persist and fire independently at nearby enemies. Placement, trap activation, repeated lightning discharge, and enemy contact are all visible during normal combat.
- readability_notes: The trap bodies are small, but their bright pulsing heads and long lightning bolts make the delegate’s location and targeting direction immediately legible. Multiple traps preserve a recognizable formation while increasing electrical clutter.

## Search log
- Searched Path of Exile shop pages, official forums, and official YouTube results for totem skins, Ballista Totem, Shockwave Totem, and Ancestral Warchief; verified Arcane Tome, Dragon, Ziggurat, and Ancestral Warchief videos, selecting the longer combat-focused skill reveal.
- Searched Diablo III’s official game guide for Sentry and its rune variants; the skill page was verified, but no accessible video showcase with dependable phase coverage surfaced, so it was omitted.
- Searched Grim Dawn’s official wiki and Mortar Trap build videos; selected the timestamped multi-encounter showcase because it covers deployment through repeated impacts.
- Searched Last Epoch official/community results for Storm, Thorn, Ballista, and Tempest Totems; results were predominantly third-party guides without a stronger isolated showcase than the selected references.
- Searched Diablo II: Resurrected Lightning Sentry showcases and build guides; selected the endgame gameplay video for sustained placement, activation, and hit coverage.
